transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because I keep getting stuck on this... this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and cheek. I just focus on it a lot, especially in photos or when I'm under the bright fluorescent lights at the store where I work. Even when other people tell me they don't really see it, it just feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me.
When you think about this spot on your nose and cheek, do you believe it's actually noticeable to other people, or do you recognize that it might not be as visible as it feels to you?

Um, I'm not really sure. Like, when my friends or my mom tell me they don't see it, I try to tell myself that maybe it isn't as bad as I think. But then... I don't know, when I'm actually looking at it in the mirror, it just looks so obvious to me. So I guess I kind of go back and forth on whether other people can actually see it or not.
Besides looking in the mirror, do you find yourself doing other things repeatedly because of this spot—like picking at it, covering it up, or asking others if they notice it?

Yeah, I do a few things. I don't really pick at it, but... when I'm on my breaks at work, I almost always end up checking my face in the bathroom mirror. I spend time fixing my hair around it, just trying to get it to fall right so it covers that spot. 

And I definitely compare myself to the girls who come through my checkout line at the store. I just look at them and notice how different they look compared to me. Sometimes I get so caught up in the bathroom checking and fixing my hair that I actually take way too long, and I end up being late getting back to the register.

When you really think about it logically, do you recognize that your worry about this spot might be out of proportion to how noticeable it actually is, or does it genuinely seem as serious and noticeable as any other significant flaw would be?

Um, I'm not really sure. Like, if I really try to think about it logically... I don't know. I guess I can't really tell if my worry is out of proportion or not. It just feels like a really big deal to me when I'm looking at it, but I don't know if it's actually as serious as I make it out to be in my head. I'm just not sure.

When you step back and think about it, do you recognize that you might be spending an unusual amount of time and energy worrying about this spot compared to how much most people would worry about a similar small mark on their face?

I mean, I don't really know how much other people worry about things like this. I guess I spend a lot of time on it, but... I don't know if it's unusual or not. It's just what I do. I haven't really thought about it compared to other people.

If I told you that most people wouldn't spend this much time checking and fixing their appearance because of a small spot on their face, would you be able to agree with that, or would you still feel like your concerns are completely justified?

I guess... I mean, if you say most people wouldn't spend this much time on it, I'd probably agree with that. It makes sense when you put it like that. But even if I know it's probably too much time, it still just feels... really important to me. Like, I still feel like I need to do it, even if other people wouldn't.

Even though you just agreed that most people wouldn't spend this much time on it, when you're actually in that moment at work looking in the mirror, can you still recognize in that moment that you're probably overdoing it, or does it feel completely necessary and reasonable to you at that time?

When I'm actually in the bathroom at work... I don't think I really step back and analyze it like that. It just feels like something I have to do right then. I guess in the moment, it feels completely necessary. I'm not really telling myself I'm overdoing it, I just... I just want to make sure it looks okay before I go back out to the register. So yeah, at the time, it just feels like something I need to do.

When you're not at work and you're just going about your day, do you ever think to yourself that maybe you're being too hard on yourself about this spot, or does it always feel like a real problem that deserves your attention?

I don't know, I guess... even when I'm just at home or running errands, it still feels like a real problem to me. I don't really sit around thinking I'm being too hard on myself. It's just... there. And it bothers me. So I guess it always feels like something I need to pay attention to, no matter where I am.

When you're not actually looking in the mirror or thinking about the spot, if you really tried to step back and think about it, could you tell yourself that maybe you're worrying too much about it, or does it still feel like a completely reasonable concern even when you're not focused on it?

I'm not really sure, honestly. Um... when I'm not actively looking in a mirror or thinking about it, I'm usually just busy with other things, like ringing people up at work or whatever. I don't think I've ever really tried to step back and ask myself that. So I don't really know if I could tell myself I'm worrying too much... I just haven't really tried to look at it that way.

If you tried really hard right now to think about it objectively, do you think the spot on your nose and cheek is actually something that most people would find noticeable and unattractive, or do you think you might be seeing it as worse than it really is?

Um... if I really try to think about it right now... I guess I'm not totally sure. It's hard to say. I mean, maybe it's possible I'm seeing it as worse than it really is? But when I look at it, it just seems so obvious to me. 

I can't really tell what other people are actually seeing when they look at me, like when I'm checking them out at the store. I just know what I see, and it looks bad to me. So... I don't really know if most people find it as noticeable or unattractive as I do. I just don't know.

When I ask you directly like this, can you recognize that your worry about this spot is probably more than it needs to be, or does it still feel completely reasonable and justified to you even when I point it out?

I mean... when you put it like that, and ask me directly, I guess I'm not really sure. I don't know if I can say for a fact that my worry is more than it needs to be. It still feels like a real problem to me, so I guess it feels justified in my head. I just... I don't know if I can look at it and say I'm definitely overreacting. It just feels like something I have to worry about.

If I were to look at your nose and cheek right now, do you think I would actually be able to see this spot that bothers you so much, or do you think it's something that's mostly noticeable to you but not really visible to other people?

I think you'd probably be able to see it if you looked closely, but... well, other people have told me they don't see it when I point it out. But that's actually why I came in today. I just keep getting stuck on this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek. It really stands out to me in photos, or when I'm working under those bright fluorescent store lights. Even if people say they don't see it, it just feels like it's the very first thing customers and my managers notice when they look at me.

When you really think about it carefully, do you believe that the way you're focused on this spot is reasonable and makes sense, or do you think it might be excessive even if it doesn't feel that way to you in the moment?

I don't really know. When I try to think about it carefully... I guess I'm just not sure. Sometimes I think maybe it is a little excessive, just because I spend so much time worrying about it. But then, it just feels so real to me. So I don't really have a clear answer for that. It just makes sense to me to worry about it, even if maybe I shouldn't.

If you were to describe this spot to a dermatologist or a completely objective stranger who had never met you before, do you think they would agree that it's a significant flaw worth worrying about the way you do, or would they likely tell you it's not really noticeable or a problem?

I honestly don't know. If I went to a dermatologist... I mean, I'd hope they would see what I'm talking about and tell me how to fix it. But based on what my friends and family say, a stranger might just tell me it's not noticeable. I guess I can't say for sure what they would think. It's just... to me, it feels significant, even if someone else might not see it that way right off the bat.

Perceived defect is not observable or appears slight to others (friends, family report not seeing it)
Preoccupation is present across multiple contexts (at work under fluorescent lights, in photos, during daily activities)
Repetitive mirror checking (multiple times during work breaks)
Repetitive grooming behavior (fixing hair to cover the spot)
Social comparison behavior (comparing self to customers at checkout)
Fluctuating insight: able to acknowledge logically when prompted that concern may be excessive, but unable to maintain this perspective in the moment
In-the-moment experience: preoccupation feels completely necessary and reasonable during active episodes
Uncertain about whether worry is proportionate to actual visibility of the defect
